pathway_name: Prebiotic cyanosulfidic photoredox synthesis of valine
pathway_type: Nonenzymatic photochemical synthesis followed by Strecker-type amino acid formation

molecules.role: Prebiotic sulfur source and photochemical reductant
Nitrogen source for amino acid synthesis

reactions.description: Formaldehyde reacts with hydrogen cyanide to form glycolonitrile.
reactions.conditions: Aqueous environment; cyanide addition to a carbonyl group

reactions.reaction_type: Photoreductive nitrile conversion and imine hydrolysis
reactions.description: Glycolonitrile undergoes UV-driven reduction of the nitrile group to an imine, followed by hydrolysis to glycolaldehyde and ammonia.
reactions.conditions: UV irradiation; aqueous hydrogen sulfide or hydrosulfide; Cu(I) cyanide photoredox catalysis
reactions.note: Reducing equivalents and sulfur-containing byproducts are not represented stoichiometrically.

reactions.description: Glycolaldehyde reacts with hydrogen cyanide to form glyceronitrile.
Glyceronitrile undergoes photoreductive nitrile conversion followed by hydrolysis to glyceraldehyde.
reactions.conditions: UV irradiation; H2S or HS- as reductant; aqueous Cu(I)-mediated photoredox chemistry

reactions.description: Glyceraldehyde isomerizes to the more stable triose ketone, dihydroxyacetone, through enolization and ketonization.
reactions.conditions: Near-neutral aqueous phosphate buffer; general acid-base catalysis

reactions.description: Dihydroxyacetone undergoes UV-driven reductive deoxygenation, producing acetone among the major products.
reactions.conditions: UV irradiation; aqueous H2S/HS-; Cu(I)-mediated photoredox chemistry
reactions.note: Glycerol is a competing product. Water and oxidized reductant byproducts are omitted.

reactions.description: Acetone reacts reversibly with hydrogen cyanide to give acetone cyanohydrin.
reactions.note: The equilibrium is relatively unfavorable compared with aldehyde cyanohydrin formation.

reactions.description: Hydrosulfide adds to the nitrile group of acetone cyanohydrin to form an alpha-hydroxythioamide.
reactions.conditions: Aqueous H2S/HS-; near-neutral pH; dark reaction before irradiation
Controlled UV irradiation; H2S-derived reducing equivalents
reactions.note: Water and oxidation byproducts are omitted.

reactions.description: Continued irradiation reduces the thioamide to the corresponding aldehyde, isobutyraldehyde.
reactions.note: The aldehyde is a transient intermediate and can undergo competing further reduction. Nitrogen- and sulfur-containing byproducts are omitted.

reactions.description: Isobutyraldehyde reacts with hydrogen cyanide to give the alpha-hydroxynitrile precursor of valine.
reactions.conditions: Aqueous HCN; in situ trapping of the aldehyde

reactions.description: Ammonia converts the alpha-hydroxynitrile into the corresponding alpha-aminonitrile, establishing valine's amino acid skeleton.
reactions.note: Formation of this valine aminonitrile was experimentally demonstrated in the referenced cyanosulfidic network.

reactions.description: Hydrolysis of the aminonitrile converts the nitrile group into a carboxylic acid, giving racemic valine.
reactions.conditions: Aqueous hydrolysis; acid or base catalysis and/or heating can accelerate the reaction
reactions.note: This is the established final hydrolysis of Strecker aminonitriles. It should not be interpreted as a direct experimental demonstration of the entire sequence under one set of early-Earth conditions.

potential_catalysts: Phosphate as an acid-base catalyst and buffer
prebiotic_context.candidate_environment: Aqueous surface pools on early Earth containing cyanide and reduced sulfur species, with periods of sunlight exposure and darkness.
prebiotic_context.evidence_assessment: The cyanohydrin-thioamide photochemical sequence and formation of the valine aminonitrile are experimentally supported. The final conversion to valine uses established Strecker nitrile hydrolysis chemistry. The complete pathway is a plausible prebiotic synthesis network, not proof of its occurrence on early Earth.
prebiotic_context.stereochemical_limitation: The nonenzymatic route does not establish a preference for L-valine and is expected to produce both D- and L-valine.
prebiotic_context.graph_semantics: The network tracks principal molecular transformations. It is not a complete atom-balanced reaction network: photons, electrons, protons, some water molecules, oxidized sulfur species, and other secondary products are omitted from individual steps.
